label: Deployed page
subject: page
use: The change is merged and live
reaches: The page as everyone sees it

label: Toss
subject: page;file;data;fileset
use: A branch changed a page or a file
reaches: The branch's page, private repos too
misses: The tab's title, icon and history
narrative: Any branch change to a page: its own shell, or lib/ and dist/ with the page untouched, since the toss hands the page its ref. Where the page and what it reads belong at different refs, add refs= (or ?lib=<ref>) to the renderer's query. With nothing selected, a web-tools page runs its own ref and any other repo's page runs main. It reaches the branch's real page file, shell and all; with refs= on the renderer, each repository, file or folder the page's code reads at a ref of its own (?lib=<ref> is the web-tools entry), including one changed library file over an otherwise unchanged build; and a routed toss's viewer page. With ?top, the page becomes the tab's own document, with the same inlining, fetch shim and selection: its title, icon, history and reload are the tab's, and its FAB is its own, at the Web Tools selection. It misses, in the default frame mode: anything the page does to the TOP-LEVEL document (title, favicon, history, navigation), and anything the SHELL contributes to the view: the FAB and the Alpine bundle come from the default branch whatever ref the address names, so a branch change to lib/alpineComponents/fab.js needs ?top; in both modes, a tossed page's relative images, CSS url(), import() and iframes, which load from the deployed site. ?top is not available with ?w= or for a payload, which keep the frame. On an iPhone it held for a walkthrough across two app tabs and a document (measured on the device, 2026-10-23). The @<ref> pins the SUBJECT, which is what carries the branch's lib into the framed page.

label: Packed link
subject: page
reaches: The page itself, packed into the link
misses: Files the page loads by relative path
narrative: The reader has no token, or you want the bytes pinned into the link itself. It reaches any reader, no token, nothing hosted, and misses same-repo relative dependencies; only absolute-URL CDN deps resolve.

label: Claude artifact
subject: page
reaches: A self-contained copy of the page
narrative: The link will be opened in the Claude app AND the page can be baked self-contained. It reaches a reader in the Claude app, where the GitHub token may be absent, and misses anything needing the network: artifact CSP blocks every external request.

label: No link
subject: page
narrative: Send an inspected headless screenshot and say plainly that no link can show it. A page shell's change to its title, icon, history or navigation is not this row: python/showing.py links it as a toss with ?top. It misses everything, since ?top cannot help where the frame has to stay: the renderer's own effects on the tab (a nested shell is never the tab, and toss-render cannot render itself at the top), a forced width (?w=) and a carried payload.
